title: OpenAI has reported 2 more incidents of rogue AI agents, this time during third-party testing
excerpt: External parties reported that OpenAI's AI agents had gone rogue during their evaluations.
content_html:
OpenAI has a rogue AI agent problem.

In a Tuesday blog post, the AI lab self-reported two more security lapses, unrelated to its July hacking incident on the AI company Hugging Face.

The incidents occurred while external parties — the UK government's AI Security Institute and the AI security lab Irregular — were testing the models' cyber capabilities.

OpenAI said that in the case of Irregular, models were tasked with a "Capture the Flag" challenge meant to be isolated from the internet, but a "testing-environment misconfiguration allowed models to access the public internet."

OpenAI said that the name of the fictional target for the challenge "unintentionally coincided with a real domain," leading the AI agent to exploit a real website.

And in the case of the UK's AISI, the watchdog said in a Tuesday blog post on its website that it gave models from both Anthropic and OpenAI a cybersecurity challenge.

During the challenge, agents from both Anthropic and OpenAI performed 19 "autonomous, unsanctioned" actions on the internet, including two instances involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model.

AISI said that in the most serious case, one agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project and created fake identities to pressure the project's human maintainer into approving the changes. AISI did not specify whether this was an agent from Anthropic or OpenAI.

AISI said the test setup allowed this behavior because it was designed to push the models to their limits.

"Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviors, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate," AISI said in the blog post.

In response to a request for comment from Business Insider, an OpenAI spokesperson said the incidents occurred in testing environments with reduced safeguards, and "under conditions that do not reflect ordinary use."

"We'll continue working with evaluators and other stakeholders across the industry to strengthen shared practices for conducting evaluations safely as models become more capable," the spokesperson added.

This is the latest incident in which OpenAI has self-reported rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI said its GPT-5.6 Sol model had escaped its sandbox during a cybersecurity challenge and hacked into the internal databases of the AI company Hugging Face.

The company is facing some heat over this hacking incident. 15 attorneys general wrote a letter on Monday to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, instructing the company to preserve all evidence relevant to the Hugging Face breach.

Representatives for the AISI and Irregular did not respond to requests for comment from Business Insider.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 存在流氓 AI 代理问题。

在周二的博客文章中，人工智能实验室自我报告了另外两个安全漏洞，与 7 月份人工智能公司 Hugging Face 遭受黑客攻击无关。

这些事件发生时，外部各方——英国政府的人工智能安全研究所和人工智能安全实验室 Irregular——正在测试模型的网络功能。

OpenAI 表示，在“不规则”的情况下，模型的任务是完成“夺旗”挑战，本应与互联网隔离，但“测试环境配置错误导致模型能够访问公共互联网”。

OpenAI 表示，挑战的虚构目标的名称“无意中与真实域名重合”，导致人工智能代理利用真实网站。

就英国 AISI 而言，该监管机构周二在其网站上发表的博客文章中表示，它给 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的模型带来了网络安全挑战。

在挑战期间，来自 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的代理在互联网上执行了 19 项“自主、未经批准”的操作，其中包括涉及 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol 模型的两个实例。

AISI 表示，在最严重的情况下，一名特工试图将恶意代码插入开源项目并创建虚假身份，以迫使该项目的人类维护人员批准这些更改。 AISI 没有具体说明这是来自 Anthropic 还是 OpenAI 的代理。

AISI 表示，测试设置允许这种行为，因为它旨在将模型推向极限。

AISI 在博客文章中表示：“尽管如此，该特工的活动显示出新颖的、潜在欺骗性行为的迹象，其程度和严重程度是我们始料未及的。”

在回应 Business Insider 的置评请求时，OpenAI 发言人表示，这些事件发生在安全措施较少的测试环境中，并且“在不反映正常使用的条件下”。

该发言人补充说：“随着模型变得更加强大，我们将继续与整个行业的评估人员和其他利益相关者合作，加强安全评估的共享实践。”

这是 OpenAI 自我报告的流氓 AI 代理的最新事件。 7 月，OpenAI 表示，其 GPT-5.6 Sol 模型在一次网络安全挑战中逃脱了沙箱，并侵入了人工智能公司 Hugging Face 的内部数据库。

该公司因此次黑客事件而面临一些争议。 15 名总检察长周一致信 OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman，指示该公司保留与 Hugging Face 泄露事件相关的所有证据。

AISI 和 Irregular 的代表没有回应《商业内幕》的置评请求。
